body: As always I'm happy to open a PR if you guide me to the right point. Currently, I think, we need to merge the `__class_getitem__ ` of Base and CommonBase

sure.   In trying to understand what's happening here, IIUC there's no regression here, because previously you couldn't use `Base[typ]` in any case.   Below illustrates if you use `Base` non generically, which was your only option previously, nothing is wrong:

```py
from typing import Generic
from typing import Type
from typing import TypeVar

from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy.orm import as_declarative


T = TypeVar("T", bound="CommonBase")  # noqa

class CommonBase(Generic[T]):
    @classmethod
    def boring(cls: Type[T]) -> Type[T]:
        return cls

@as_declarative()
class Base(CommonBase[T]):
    pass

class Tab1(Base):
    __tablename__ = "foo"
    a = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

class Tab2(Base["Tab"]):
    __tablename__ = "bar"
    a = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)

assert Tab1.__table__ is not None  # fine
assert Tab2.__table__ is not None  # AttributeError 
```

can you confirm we didn't break anything for anyone here?
@zzzeek yes, the example works as you said. W/o generics everything is fine, so no regression
cool.  I would welcome a PR w/ a new test + a changelog file.

I would place a breakpoint() statement into the `__class_getitem__()` method and see what the interpreter is passing there as well as what it's expecting to see as a result, in order to produce the desired behavior.

`class Tab(Base, metaclass=DeclarativeMeta):` work fine, but `class Tab(Base["Tab"], metaclass=DeclarativeMeta)` fails:

issue.title: Fix missing class attributes when using __class_getitem__
issue.body:
Closes #7462

### Description
As discussed in #7462, the normal `__class_getitem__` of `typing.Generics` leads to issues, so that the metaclass of the declarative base is not applied to child classes of it. Therefore we replace it with an own imlementation.
